verification_scope_reason: Actual fixed Source Sharp and native Pillow encode controlled PNG fixtures at exact long-edge request targets, including the 1224x1429 to 1187x1386 rounded edge, thin/wide/tall shapes, no enlargement, alpha and unreachable byte targets. Metadata, original-byte reuse, cache repair, cancellation identity and target-complete digest relationships are compared. Byte values/digests are compared only within the owning codec. Native current-provider concurrent requests prove same-target sharing, distinct-target generations and durable-source preservation. Canonical Messages pricing/serialization, current attachment and historical combined HTTP upload consumers pass.
activation_boundary: The mounted current attachment provider now accepts width/height/maxBytes targets. New Pillow target variants use request-image-pillow-10.4-v2-target; width, height and byte budget all enter the key. Sharp identities remain separate. The previous maxPixels capability remains explicitly compatible for frozen historical consumers during composition migration; the legacy adapter dispatch helper converts its pixel policy to a target for current async providers.
limits: Metadata/behavior equivalence does not establish encoded-byte equality between Sharp and Pillow. The split authenticated Messages/Files transport remains subsequent work. No full regression or release acceptance is claimed.
